correctness.rationale: The rational projector trace is N/s. Generic numerator Wronskians have 4n−2 simple finite zeros; the normalized weighted-two-square subfamily of projector data dominates P(C[t]_{≤2n}) by a full-rank differential, proved using coprime f,g and a coefficient-dot-product orthogonality argument. Generic f,g avoid cuts by independent nonzero polynomial resultants. The finite-field checker confirms 18 nondegenerate examples but is not relied upon for the all-n,d conclusion.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly computes ED degree and discusses GD for projector data. Its ED formula subsumes only the numerical value as a possible upper bound, not equality for generic projector-constrained data or exclusion of the cut locus. The differential-dominance lemma is not implied merely by the ED calculation. Relevant searches and full primary-text comparisons did not locate equivalent coverage; residual literature-priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: An unlocated general theorem proving ED/GD equality for projector curves may subsume the claim.

value.rationale: For a standard infinite family of scrolls and all ranks d≥2, proves that constraining the data to Grassmannian projectors does not remove any generic Euclidean critical points, settles their generic cut-locus status, and supplies a usable geometric mechanism explaining equality. This is a motivated enumerative invariant identified in contemporary work, not a numerical re-tabulation.
